newsitem.title: CANADA: BOC's Thiessen says confidence in dollar crucial.
newsitem.headline: BOC's Thiessen says confidence in dollar crucial.

text.p: Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen said on Wednesday that recent weakness in the Canadian dollar would wane as the country's economy approached full capacity.

"As we get back toward full capacity, some of the current weakness in our Canadian dollar is going to disappear," said Thiessen. "I believe that the underlying trend in the Canadian dollar is upwards."

The central bank head also said the Bank of Canada had no set target for the currency but closely monitored the effect of currency movements on the Canadian economy, including the stimulus effect of a weak dollar on the economy.

"Obviously there are some movements that are going to end up being too stimulative for the Canadian economy and we will feel obliged to respond to that. It's also true that it is absolutely crucial to maintain confidence in your currency," said Thiessen.
Thiessen said the fact that Canadian interest rates were lower than U.S. rates as far out as 10 years on the yield curve reflected investor optimism regarding the currency.
